ksmscl_real_procurement_cycle_timeline.description: Table 4.2: real dates of each stage of KSMSCL's annual procurement cycle (State Therapeutic Committee meeting -> indent submission -> Need Assessment Committee meeting -> government approval -> tender -> purchase order issuance), 2016-17 to 2021-22. No fixed calendar schedule existed for this cycle (the audit's own finding), which is WHY real cycle lengths vary so widely -- this is the actual, documented mechanism a real deployment's redistribution/reorder timing would need to model, not an assumption we invented.

ksmscl_real_procurement_cycle_timeline.note: Full cycle length = committee-meeting date to purchase-order-issuance date, in real calendar days, for the 5 years where a PO date exists. Used directly (not a made-up range) as the empirical distribution for how long a procurement disruption realistically lasts once triggered -- see scripts/generate_synthetic_stock.py.

essential_drug_availability_shortage_by_.description: As of the audit snapshot date (30 June 2022): all test-checked District Hospitals (DH) had fewer than 50 of the 128 required Essential Drug List (EDL) items; Taluk Hospitals (TH) had at most 35 of 81; CHCs had at most 25 of 64.

thalassemia_deferoxamine_shortage.description: Desferal (Deferoxamine) injection, the standard iron-chelation drug for thalassemia patients, has been absent from Karnataka government hospital shelves since the 2020 COVID-19 outbreak. This is a persistent, multi-year, legally-contested shortage -- a different failure pattern from a crisis-and-recovery arc, documented across three real, dated sources below. Deferoxamine is NOT on the NLEM 2022 essential-drug list (verified: absent from data/processed/nlem_catalog.json) -- its absence from the essential-drugs list is arguably why it fell out of the state's own procurement priority. Included in this project because of these real, dated, named sources, not because it is one of our NLEM-sourced Tier-1 drugs.
